analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is a B2B wind O&M services company with a 1.02% ROE, negative 7-year revenue CAGR, and a P/E of 81.6x — there is no value here by any measure I use. A business that has been loss-making for most of its history and only earned INR 22 Cr on a INR 6,549 Cr market cap is speculation, not investment.
key_strengths: Debt dramatically reduced from INR 1,411 Cr (2021) to INR 95 Cr (2025) — D/E now 0.05, balance sheet cleaned up
Promoter holding at 56.12% — reasonable skin in the game
Operating margin of ~15% shows the core O&M service business has decent unit economics
key_risks: Catastrophic returns: ROE of 1.02% and ROCE of 2.60% — destroying value at current valuation of 81.6x P/E and 129x EV/EBITDA
Revenue CAGR of -6.1% over 7 years; net profit already shrinking in just its second profitable year (INR 28 Cr → INR 22 Cr)
Fully captive to parent Inox Wind Limited — no independent business moat, growth entirely dependent on parent's order execution
red_flags: P/E of 81.6x and EV/EBITDA of 129x for a company with ROE barely above 1% — extreme overvaluation
Net profit declining in FY25 (INR 22 Cr vs INR 28 Cr) despite only two years of profitability after a decade of losses
INR 637 Cr investing outflow in FY25 funded by INR 572 Cr equity raise — aggressive capital-intensive expansion at poor returns
Historically negative free cash flow (FCF positive in only 3 of 5 years); cumulative losses eroded equity to near-zero before IPO equity infusion
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is not the kind of business I invest in. My entire philosophy is built around predictable, consumer-facing businesses with strong returns on capital — businesses where the underlying economics are simple, durable, and compound quietly. Inox Green fails every single screen. ROE of 1.02% means the business earns almost nothing on shareholders' money. ROCE of 2.60% is below the cost of capital. Yet the market prices this at 81.6x earnings and 22x revenue. That is pure speculation on a renewable energy theme, not investing.

The financial history is deeply concerning. The company lost money every single year from 2018 through 2023. Revenue in 2025 (INR 236 Cr) is actually lower than 2018 (INR 368 Cr). EBITDA is in a contracting trend. The balance sheet cleanup via debt reduction is the only bright spot, but it was funded by equity dilution at the IPO — not organic cash generation. The FY25 investing outflow of INR 637 Cr funded by a INR 572 Cr equity raise shows they are burning fresh capital for expansion before proving the existing business can earn adequate returns. I will not pay 81x for a business with a 1% ROE and a parent-dependent model. Hard avoid.
